docket_opinion: Base ROE set in 2006 order (Docket EL04-108 lineage)
methodology: Litigated/settlement-based base ROE predating FERC's modern two-step DCF framework
notes: Base ROE in effect for New England Transmission Owners (NETOs) until challenged by a 2011 customer complaint.

methodology: Two-step DCF model (short- and long-term growth, 33% weight to long-term GDP growth); ROE set at midpoint of upper half of the DCF zone of reasonableness
notes: Reduced NETO base ROE from 11.14% following the September 2011 FPA Section 206 complaint. Later vacated in part by the D.C. Circuit in Emera Maine v. FERC (2017), which found FERC had not adequately justified the new ROE or its methodology.

methodology: Two-step DCF model + CAPM composite zone of reasonableness; midpoint used because NETOs found to be of 'average risk'
notes: Issued after ~15 years of litigation across four stacked complaints. Retroactively applied back to October 16, 2014, ordering NETOs to refund ratepayers an estimated $1.5 billion (with interest) by May 20, 2027.
Base ROE used by most Midcontinent ISO (MISO) transmission owners since 2002, until challenged by a November 2013 FPA Section 206 complaint.

docket_opinion: Order applying Opinion No. 531 framework (Docket EL14-12)
methodology: Two-step DCF model, consistent with the Opinion No. 531 methodology developed in the NETO case
notes: First reduction of MISO TOs' base ROE, prompted by the 2013 complaint. Vacated by the D.C. Circuit a year later after it found the same flaws as in the NETO case.

methodology: DCF, CAPM, and risk premium models combined into a composite zone of reasonableness; midpoint used
notes: Reissued after the D.C. Circuit vacated the 2016 MISO order following Emera Maine. Restored the risk premium model to the analysis (on rehearing in Opinion No. 569-A) after initially dropping it.

methodology: DCF and CAPM only (risk premium model dropped again); composite zone midpoint
notes: Refunds ordered for the Nov 2013-Feb 2015 and Sept 2016-Oct 2024 periods. Upheld by the D.C. Circuit on appeal.

docket_opinion: Baseline formula-rate ROE prior to complaint (AEP's SPP-zone subsidiaries)
notes: Base ROE embedded in AEP's four SPP-zone transmission-owning subsidiaries' formula rate before East Texas Electric Cooperative and others filed an FPA Section 206 complaint on June 5, 2017.

docket_opinion: Settlement Agreement accepted by FERC (ER20-928 lineage)
methodology: Negotiated settlement following FPA Section 206 complaint
notes: FERC accepted a settlement between AEP and East Texas Electric Cooperative reducing AEP's SPP-zone base ROE from 10.70% to 10.00%, effective June 5, 2017 (the complaint date), with refunds.

methodology: Individual formula rates per company -- SPP has no single RTO-wide base ROE
notes: Per S&P Global Market Intelligence, base ROEs across SPP's transmission owners have been unchanged since the 2020 AEP settlement, ranging from 9.72% (Xcel Energy's PSCo) to 10.80% (Prairie Wind Transmission), excluding incentive adders.

methodology: Individual formula rates per company (PJM OATT Attachment H) -- no single RTO-wide base ROE
notes: PJM has no generic RTO-wide base-ROE complaint case comparable to NETO/MISO. Each of PJM's ~26 transmission owners sets its own base ROE via its own formula rate. As of ~2025, base ROEs ranged from 9.80% (MAIT) to 11.20% (TrAILCo); most companies also carry a common 50 bp RTO-participation adder, and 10 companies carry additional project-specific adders of 25-150 bp.

docket_opinion: PG&E transmission owner rate case (Docket ER19-13 lineage)
notes: FERC rejected PG&E's requested 13.3% transmission ROE and set base ROE at 9.3%, appropriate for a utility of average risk, for the rate year beginning March 1, 2017. CAISO participating TOs (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E) are regulated individually like PJM/SPP, not via one CAISO-wide base ROE; FERC separately denied PG&E a 50 bp RTO-participation adder after a 2022 California law made CAISO membership mandatory, a denial upheld by the Ninth Circuit in July 2025.

docket_opinion: Baseline OATT base ROE prior to complaint (Docket EL18-147 lineage)
notes: Base ROE in the Southern Company traditional operating companies' (Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Gulf Power, Mississippi Power) joint Open Access Transmission Tariff before Alabama Municipal Electric Authority and Cooperative Energy filed an FPA Section 206 complaint in 2018. Southern Company is not a member of an RTO/ISO for its transmission function.

docket_opinion: Settlement Agreement accepted by FERC (Docket ER19-1427 lineage)
methodology: Negotiated settlement following FPA Section 206 complaint
notes: FERC accepted a settlement among Southern Company Services, AMEA, and Cooperative Energy reducing the OATT base ROE from 11.25% to 10.60%, effective May 10, 2018 (the refund effective date). The settlement also imposed a 5-year moratorium barring either side from filing to change the ROE again.

docket_opinion: Policy Statement on ROE and proxy groups (no docket-specific number)
methodology: Equal weighting of DCF and CAPM models; risk premium model excluded for pipelines due to insufficient data; clarified proxy group formation rules (incl. Canadian companies)
notes: Not a numeric base ROE for a single pipeline -- a generic policy statement guiding how ROE is calculated in individual gas/oil pipeline rate cases going forward.
